verses.1: Now the young mock me, and I, who used to revere their fathers, now they treat me as a stranger, like a foreign shepherd.
verses.2: What good is the strength of their hands to me? Their whole livelihood has withered away.
verses.3: They are hungry and thirsty, withered like desert wastelands. They are driven from one place to another, groaning under a burden they cannot carry.
verses.4: They gather salt from thorny plants, and their food comes from the roots of ragged plants.
verses.5: Driven from their homes, they live in caves and in holes in the ground like thieves.
verses.6: They dwell among streams, in the clefts of rocks, and in the ruins of the earth.
verses.7: They live among shrubs, they lie beneath the bushes in the wasteland.
verses.8: They are fools and the nameless, and their memory is blotted out from the land.
verses.9: But now I am their music, and I am a proverb to them.
verses.10: They despise me and keep their distance from me; they do not refrain from spitting in my face.
verses.11: For he opened his bow and shot arrows at me, and he loosed the bridle from my face.
verses.12: Their right hand pierced me, they spread out their feet to trip me, and they laid their paths for my destruction.
verses.13: They plundered my paths, they stripped me of my cloak.
verses.14: They poured out arrows like a wide stream; under the threat of destruction, they hurled me down.
verses.15: My prosperity turned back on me like a storm, my hope was swept away like the wind, and my salvation passed like a cloud.
verses.16: Now my soul is poured out over me, and days of suffering seize me.
verses.17: At night my bones are shattered, and my sinews do not rest.
verses.18: By great strength, they stripped me of my clothing, as a tunic they took from me and clothed me in ashes.
verses.19: I was cast down to the dust and ashes.
verses.20: I cried out to you, but you did not answer; I stood and you paid no attention to me.
verses.21: You turned into my enemy, with a strong hand you drove me away.
verses.22: You lifted me up in the wind, you whirled me about, and cast me into ruin.
verses.23: For I know that death will bring me back, and the tent of every living being is the grave.
verses.24: Yet if I had any power to help myself, or if I had sought aid from another, I would have found it.
verses.25: But I did weep for the suffering of the poor, I groaned when I saw the afflicted man.
verses.26: For I expected good things, but evil came. I waited for light, but came darkness.
verses.27: My bowels are boiled without rest; days of suffering overtook me.
verses.28: I walked about in agony, without comfort; I stood in the assembly and cried out.
verses.29: I was like a brother to jackals, like a companion to ostriches.
verses.30: My skin turned black on me, and my bones burned from the heat.
verses.31: My lyre became a dirge for me, and my harp a voice of weeping.

notes:
Notes
- v. 8: "nameless" is a rendering of בְּלִי־שֵׁם, which literally means "without name," used here to describe the despised and forgotten.
- v. 9: "music" is a rendering of קִתָֽרָה, referring to a musical instrument, used metaphorically here to describe how Job is now a source of mockery for the young.
- v. 18: "clothed me in ashes" reflects the Hebrew metaphor of being stripped and then clothed in shame and ruin, with ashes symbolizing mourning and humiliation.

[1] Now the young mock me, and I, who used to revere their fathers, now they treat me as a stranger, like a foreign shepherd.

[2] What good is the strength of their hands to me? Their whole livelihood has withered away.

[3] They are hungry and thirsty, withered like desert wastelands. They are driven from one place to another, groaning under a burden they cannot carry.

[4] They gather salt from thorny plants, and their food comes from the roots of ragged plants.

[5] Driven from their homes, they live in caves and in holes in the ground like thieves.

[6] They dwell among streams, in the clefts of rocks, and in the ruins of the earth.

[7] They live among shrubs, they lie beneath the bushes in the wasteland.

[8] They are fools and the nameless, and their memory is blotted out from the land.

[9] But now I am their music, and I am a proverb to them.

[10] They despise me and keep their distance from me; they do not refrain from spitting in my face.

[11] For he opened his bow and shot arrows at me, and he loosed the bridle from my face.

[12] Their right hand pierced me, they spread out their feet to trip me, and they laid their paths for my destruction.

[13] They plundered my paths, they stripped me of my cloak.

[14] They poured out arrows like a wide stream; under the threat of destruction, they hurled me down.

[15] My prosperity turned back on me like a storm, my hope was swept away like the wind, and my salvation passed like a cloud.

[16] Now my soul is poured out over me, and days of suffering seize me.

[17] At night my bones are shattered, and my sinews do not rest.

[18] By great strength, they stripped me of my clothing, as a tunic they took from me and clothed me in ashes.

[19] I was cast down to the dust and ashes.

[20] I cried out to you, but you did not answer; I stood and you paid no attention to me.

[21] You turned into my enemy, with a strong hand you drove me away.

[22] You lifted me up in the wind, you whirled me about, and cast me into ruin.

[23] For I know that death will bring me back, and the tent of every living being is the grave.

[24] Yet if I had any power to help myself, or if I had sought aid from another, I would have found it.

[25] But I did weep for the suffering of the poor, I groaned when I saw the afflicted man.

[26] For I expected good things, but evil came. I waited for light, but came darkness.

[27] My bowels are boiled without rest; days of suffering overtook me.

[28] I walked about in agony, without comfort; I stood in the assembly and cried out.

[29] I was like a brother to jackals, like a companion to ostriches.

[30] My skin turned black on me, and my bones burned from the heat.

[31] My lyre became a dirge for me, and my harp a voice of weeping.
